summary: Palmo Kyi works in the field of Tibetology. She studied under supervisor Per Kværne (attested 2012) as well as teachers Hanna Havnevik and Rinzin Thargyal.

Pamela D. Winfield specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She held a post at Temple University (attested 2001) and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Elon University (attested 2015–2017).

Pamela Gutman (1944–2015) specialized in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She was educated at the University of Vienna and the Australian National University, where she was a research student from around 1972 to 1976.

Panahaduwe Yasassi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He was appointed Professor in Buddhist Civilization at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura in 2020 and Venerable Professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Pandurang Vaman Kane (1880–1972) was an Indology and history scholar educated at Wilson College and the University of Mumbai. He held teaching posts at Elphinstone College and Wilson College, and served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1947–1949).

Pankaj Tandon specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at St. Stephen's College, Delhi School of Economics, and Harvard University under mentor Tom Mallon-McCorgray, he became an Associate Professor at Boston University in 1978.

Paolo Daffinà (d. 2009) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and history. He studied at Sapienza University of Rome under Giuseppe Tucci, Luciano Petech, and Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale, later serving there as Professor and Director (1973–1982).

Paolo Emilio Pavolini (1864–1942) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Emilio Teza, Albrecht Weber, and Richard Pischel. He served as Professore ordinario at the University of Florence (1895–1935) and Visiting Professor at the University of Helsinki (1935–1936).

Paolo Visigalli is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sapienza University of Rome, the University of Padua, and the University of Cambridge (~2011–2016), later holding posts at NYU Shanghai (~2017–2021) and Shanghai Normal University (~2021).

Paramahansa Yogananda (1893–1952) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Scottish Church College (~1911–1913), Serampore College (~1913–1915), and the University of Calcutta (~1913–1915).

Paramita Paul works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, history, and archaeology. She earned her PhD from Leiden University in 2009 and has held posts as Lecturer at Amsterdam University College and Chief Editor at the International Institute for Asian Studies.

Parashuram Lakshman Vaidya (1891–1978) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Louis de La Vallée Poussin. He served as Director at Mithila Institute and General Editor of the Mahabharata at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

Paride Stortini is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Ca' Foscari University, University of Padua, Pontifical University Antonianum, and University of Chicago, later holding postdoctoral posts at the University of Tokyo and Ghent University.

Parimal G. Patil is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who completed studies at Harvard University and the University of Chicago (~1993–2002). Around 2001, he became a Professor at Harvard University.

Parul Dave-Mukherji works in Indology, philosophy, and history and archaeology. She completed her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (1986–1991) under Alexis Sanderson and held a professorship at Jawaharlal Nehru University (2006–2026).

Pascale Haag (born 1965) specializes in Indology and linguistics. She completed PhDs under Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat at Sorbonne Nouvelle University and Marie-Claire Gay at Paris Nanterre University, and became Associate Professor at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences in 2003.

Pascale Hugon specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. She held posts at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2006), the University of Lausanne (attested 2006–2008), and the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2008).

Pataraporn Sirikanchana specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She earned a Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania and served as a Professor at Thammasat University (attested 2012).

Patrice Ladwig is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He has held positions at the University of Bristol, the Max Planck Institute for Social Anthropology (attested 2012), and the Max Planck Society (Senior Research Fellow, 2016).

Patricia Berger is a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who earned her Ph.D. at UC Berkeley under Mark Elliott and Steven D. Goodman. She was Curator at the Asian Art Museum and became Professor Emerita at UC Berkeley.
